requirement: The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The implementation covers both obligations and is marked completely. The tests cover the main cases.

**Implementation (all in `src/lib.rs`)**

- **Shields.io URL encoding.**
  - `shield_path_component` (lines 539–552, marked `{impl}`) keeps only ASCII letters, digits and `.` unchanged.
  - Space becomes `_`, `_` becomes `__`, `-` becomes `--`, and every other byte (including all non-ASCII bytes) becomes `%XX`.
  - Characters such as `/`, `?`, `#`, `%`, `&`, `<` and `>` therefore cannot change the badge URL structure.
  - `shield_badge` (lines 522–537, marked `{impl}`) passes both label and message through this encoder.
- **HTML escaping.**
  - `shield_badge` also escapes the full URL, so `&` becomes `&`, and escapes the `alt` text with `escape_html`.
  - `escape_html` (lines 891–905, marked `{impl}`) escapes `& < > " '`.
- **Requirement names and link targets.**
  - `replace_definitions` escapes the full name in the `id` attribute (`escaped_name`) and escapes the detail `href`, both in the badge anchor and in the "See evidence" link.
  - It builds its badge through `shield_badge`.
  - `reference_badge` escapes `href` through `chapter_href` and `escape_html`. It also escapes the built-in's hover `title`, and builds its badge through `shield_badge`.
  - The `{impl}` marker in `replace_definitions` sits on the escaping statement inside the function.
  - The comment there honestly notes that valid names currently contain no special characters, so this is defensive.
- **Other uses of `shield_badge`.** The evidence-state badge in `index.rs` `render_detail_sections` goes through the same function and so gets the same encoding. The other `escape_html` uses I found (`commands.rs`, `fixme.rs`, `index.rs` input rendering) escape ordinary text rather than badge HTML.
- **Marking.** I found no badge-HTML-inserting code without an `{impl}` reference. I found no behavior beyond the requirement.

**Tests (all marked `{test}`)**

- `badge_urls_percent_encode_punctuation_and_html_is_escaped` checks an adversarial label and message: `/ ? # % & < > " '`, a space and a non-ASCII `é`. It asserts the exact encoded URL, including `&` before `labelColor`, and the escaped `alt` text.
- `reference_link_targets_are_escaped` renders a chapter whose rendered path contains `& " < >` and a space. It asserts that the `href` is escaped and that no raw `"q"` or `<x>` appears.
- `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names` checks that `_` and `-` are doubled and that a space becomes `_` in the state badge.

The tests cover punctuation, non-ASCII input, doubled separators, HTML attribute escaping and link-target escaping. One small gap: no test feeds a hostile name into the `id` attribute in `replace_definitions`. That is acceptable because names are validated and the escaping is a one-line call to the tested `escape_html`.
